title: Hardness of Sharp Intervention Bounds in Relational Causal Models with a Fixed Schema
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound result incremental below the field floor: paper-score ceiling 6.4 < 7.4, with no bounded same-topic repair.
gap_reasons: Its pathwidth-two result and fixed-gap result belong to different branches, so it does not establish fixed-gap hardness at pathwidth two.
The polynomial-time untied formulas concern only these compiler images, and there is no tractability or complexity classification for general untied instances.
The growing count addresses, exact source laws, and absence of a substantive application limit the projected leading-econometrics-journal score despite the genuine hardness contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved exact sharp endpoints and two sound NP-hardness branches for one fixed recursive binary RSCM schema, strengthening the construction to positive source and target trees, occurrence cap three, and a bounded-3DM3 fixed additive gap. The field-tier claim collapsed because pathwidth two and fixed-gap hardness occur on separate compiler families and the easy untied comparison is not a general classification. A future re-anchored project would need a new combined reduction, a general untied-instance theorem, or a substantive causal application rather than a local repair.
tldr: One fixed recursive four-type, six-role binary relational schema has two complementary hard compiler images. The SUBSET SUM branch gives an exact sharp intervention endpoint with a positive source tree and target tree, row occurrence at most three, and a quadratic pathwidth-two polynomial. The bounded-incidence three-set branch retains the same schema and source-tree and target-tree promises, uses a 36-row evaluator table and a quadratic with interaction maximum degree six, and gives a fixed additive yes/no gap ruling out a PTAS unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\). Fully untying occurrences gives explicit, strictly smaller lower endpoints.
gap: Relational identification explains transfer of supported contexts, and general causal or parametric hardness is known, but the exact cost of optimizing unsupported shared rows under the simultaneous positive-source, fixed-schema, bounded-occurrence, and sparse-polynomial restrictions is not established by the inspected results. In particular, Khajavirad's sparse quadratic algorithm does not settle this family: its nonconvexity condition holds with \(\kappa_C=0\), but the required modified-graph treewidth grows as \(n-1\).
fill: Prove the compiler correspondence and exact endpoint for every SUBSET SUM input, then give the exact fully untied relaxation value; retain the weak NP-hardness and compact-input scope.
